decision.summary: Two regions warrant closer inspection: (1) a multi-week period (485–544) with divergent trends in N (downward) and E (upward), possibly indicating sustained deformation or drift without clear reversal; (2) a sharp, coherent multi-axis shift at the very end (725–729), likely a temporary offset or data anomaly given its abruptness and cross-axis consistency.

regions.observation: N-component shows a sustained downward trend beginning around index 480, with a possible platform or pause near 510–525 before resuming decline; E-component exhibits a gradual monotonic rise from ~index 485 onward, with no clear opposing return yet visible. U-component remains noisy but shows a subtle upward bias after ~490.

From ~725 onward, all three components (N, E, U) show abrupt, coherent linear shifts over just 4–5 samples: N drops sharply (~−0.5), E rises sharply (~+0.5), U drops sharply (~−0.5), forming a triangular transient that may indicate a temporary offset or instrumental artifact; the surrounding context (720–724) is relatively stable, making this multi-axis jump stand out.
